2. Heard Sri Rupesh Srivastava, holding brief of Sri Sanjeev Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ram Mohit Yadav, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 253 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act Police Station Harpur Budhat, District Gorakhpur, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: D.P. Act Police Station Harpur Budhat
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed as there is no time of offence mentioned in it.

It is next stated that the applicant had gone to Haryana Anil Beldar vs State Of U.P. on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175865878/
1 and was doing job there.

entities.text: Haryana Anil Beldar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The cause of death has been found to be asphyxia as a result of ante mortem hanging.

The applicant has no criminal history and he is cooperating in trial.
5.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail on the ground that the deceased had expired within the precincts of house of the applicant within three years of her marriage, as such he is not entitled for bail.
6.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the deceased had expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant and there being no evidence of alibi of the applicant coupled by the fact that the deceased had expired within three years of her marriage, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
7. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

8. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

sentences.text: 9. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
